newsitem.title: CHINA: HK's Hang Seng leaps to record high in early trade.
newsitem.headline: HK's Hang Seng leaps to record high in early trade.

text.p: Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index leaped 188 points or 1.14 percent to a new record high of 16,730 just after the open on Thursday morning.
The index continued to soar to 16,747.48 before pulling back slightly to 16,734.
Big gains were seen in all blue chip sectors, with the exception of utilities, while red chips outperformed the broad market. H shares were also well bid up.
After 15 minutes, turnover was HK$3.5 billion.
Brokers said the market was still advancing on momentum and themes generated by the Cheung Kong group's acquisition of shares in Hong Kong Land and Jardine Matheson.
"Property investment companies are still undervalued," said Adrian Ngan, director at Peregrine Securities. "Property developers look fairly valued."

Brokers said that following Amoy Properties' eight percent rise on Wednesday, investors and traders would focus on other investment property companies such as Henderson Investment, Kerry Properties and others.
Amoy Properties gained HK$0.25 to HK$10.00 and Henderson Investment inched ahead HK$0.05 to HK$9.10. Kerry Properties jumped HK$0.55 to HK$21.00.
Cheung Kong soared HK$2.75 to HK$94.75.
The industrial and commercial sector led the market higher from the open. Hutchison Whampoa leaped to a new high of HK$83.00 then eased to trade up HK$0.25 at HK$81.50.
"Hutchison has roughly a gross cash level of HK$26 billion on hand and the market is trying to guess what they are going to do next," said analyst Carl Wong at HSBC James Capel.
Swire Pacific rose to an all-time high of HK$77.00 before easing to trade HK$0.75 higher at HK$75.75. The company will report its first half earnings later on Thursday.
Cathay Pacific, which reported a 35 percent drop in profit in the first half compared with the first six months of 1996, slipped HK$0.60 to HK$13.40.
Red chip China Resources added HK$0.60 to HK$38.50.
